Credits, licences and what the app connects to

JS8-Tactical, by S2 Underground. Free software under the GNU General Public License v3: you may use, share and change it under that licence, and its source code is available under the same licence.

Built on JS8Call (Jordan Sherer, KN4CRD) and JS8Android (Punk Kaos and contributors), both GPLv3.

Includes:
• Hamlib, radio control (LGPL 2.1)
• FFTW3 (GPL 2 or later)
• Oboe audio (Apache 2.0)
• MapLibre Native maps (BSD 2-clause)
• llama.cpp on-device AI (MIT)
• SBC audio codec from HTCommander, for the UV-Pro (Apache 2.0)
• AndroidX and Material Components (Apache 2.0)

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), served by OpenFreeMap. Optional AI models (Qwen2.5, Apache 2.0) are downloaded only if you choose to.

What it connects to: map tiles while the map is open; NOAA space-weather data for propagation; the AI model download if you start one; PSKReporter and the ATAK bridge only if you turn them on. Everything else stays on this device. No accounts, no analytics.

Bug reports: Settings → Diagnostics → Share diagnostic report, or email js8tactical@proton.me.

JS8-Tactical sends Cursor-on-Target points over UDP. Pick where they go in "Send to":

• This device (port 4242): ATAK on this phone or tablet. In ATAK: Settings → Network Preferences → Network Connection Preferences → Manage Inputs. Make sure an input with address 0.0.0.0, port 4242, protocol UDP exists and is ticked (add one with ⋮ → Add if not).

• Mesh SA (239.2.3.1:6969): ATAK listens here out of the box, so no ATAK setup. Every TAK device on the same Wi-Fi or mesh network sees the points too, so only use it when you mean to share them.

• Custom: another device's IP address and its UDP input port, or a TAK Server's UDP CoT input.

Then tap "Send a test point". A cyan dot named "JS8-Tactical test" should appear near your grid square within a few seconds and vanish after 5 minutes.

Points are spot-map dots: red = emergency or RED, yellow = needs or AMBER, green = good or GREEN, magenta = SPOT and SALUTE reports, cyan = other reports. Tap one in ATAK to read the whole report. Location precision follows what was sent, so a 4-character grid square gives a wide error circle.
